claim: AI is coming for the paycheck and crypto is about to have the biggest run-up in history, so turn your paycheck into ownership now, while you still have one.
why_this_claim: It is the longform's own thesis in Mike's own locked words. It runs on conviction, not data: no number, ticker, price or chart is needed to land it, so it survives the 9:16 crop and the loss of the other ten minutes. Each span does one job: the stakes (the entry-level door, then paychecks for anyone), the opportunity (an economic explosion and a crypto run-up never seen in history) and the action (own things that keep producing, now). The hook's promise (altcoins you can hold and stack) is deliberately left open, and the CTA sends the viewer to the full video to close it. The four tokens are the longform's payoff, not this short's.

assembled_read: I want to talk about some of the altcoins that you can hold and stack so you can potentially retire early. The entry level door is closing first. It'll be very difficult for anyone to get a paycheck regardless of skill level. But with that said, I do believe that we are about to have an enormous economic explosion and likewise a crypto run up that we have never experienced throughout all of history. Own things that keep producing when your job doesn't and do it now while you still have that paycheck. [CTA] Click below to WATCH the full video.

rejected.reason: 'Wages are what the AI takeover takes away. Ownership is what's left standing. So this video is about what to own.' This is the best-written line in the video, but it plays over H0, a full-frame two-word type card (WAGES / OWNERSHIP) that does not survive a 608 px centre crop (brief: no text cards). 'So this video is about what to own' is also a whole-video line. If Mike accepts the card under a crop, the first two sentences (35.38-39.54, ~4.2 s) could replace span 2.

'This could be our last chance to make it rich because it could be very, very difficult in the coming years.' The hottest line, but it does not fit: hook + body + it + kicker = 33.9 s. Swapping it in for the kicker (26.0 s) would end the short on a downer instead of the action, and would make the short all one F1 shot. It also starts on the 28.967 leak and ends inside the F1 face-out film burn (34.77-35.50).

'If you watched my previous video then you'll know that there is an enormous amount of jobs that will very very soon become obsolete.' It points at another video, and there is no trough before 'there is' to cut in at (desilenced, 0 s Whisper gaps). The paycheck sentence carries the same stakes in 4.6 s.

F2: 'Employment is still 4.2% so paychecks still exist right now. So that's exactly the window you need to turn a paycheck into ownership.' This is market data. Mike says 'Employment' (the longform caption was corrected to 'Unemployment'; the short's captions follow the spoken words). 'That's exactly the window' needs the 4.2% clause. The kicker makes the same call to action with no number.

The CH1 receipts (Challenger 120K cuts, Stanford 19%, BLS 52.8%, Amodei 'half of all entry level white collar jobs'). Market data on receipts and a real chart: the brief says hype over data, and receipts and charts do not survive a 9:16 crop.
'And it's not just a crypto guy saying this' opens on 'this' (fails the cold read), and CLIP-2 is a third party's voice.

F6 Kaspa: 'Nobody can print it. Nobody can freeze it. And nobody can change the schedule.' A great declarative hammer, but a different claim (Kaspa's architecture), and 'it' needs Kaspa named first. A candidate lead for a Kaspa-only short.
F5: 'But I can say that I just bought some ARB for the first time. So you know where I stand.' Token-specific, it travels with 'never financial advice', and it is off the one claim.
The Kaspa ('cleanest version ... my primary asset'), TAO and TON verdicts are conditional token calls. Each needs its own chapter, so a short built on one becomes a list teaser, not one claim.
F8 TAO: 'Owning TAO, or staking into a subnet, is a claim on that production, not a wage from it.' On theme (ownership vs wage), but it leans on token jargon (subnet, production) that needs CH4.

'Four different bets on the same idea.' over IMG-22 (four coins), prepended to the kicker. It would take the kicker's in-point off the film burn and add an AI still, but 'four different bets' has no referent cold (the short never names four), so it fails section 3.3.
The CTA screen share (community pitch, the 1,000 to 350,000 LAB example). An as-filmed screen share that no 9:16 crop survives, a sales pitch, and a past call.

Frames at 2.5 s, 22 s and 611 s of the FINAL show the face at ~47-52%. Cropping the comp render at the json's 58.2% would put Mike's face at the crop's left edge. Window 11 reads 90.15% because its samples are the screen-share webcam, and a crop there would miss the face entirely. Measure the crop on the comp render for spans 1, 3 and 4, or crop at ~50%.

'retire early' is spoken in the hook. The screenplay's DO-NOT-AIR note banned it as a promise, but Mike locked these exact words at GATE 1 and they aired in the delivered longform, and 'potentially' keeps it conditional. Keep it out of on-screen promise text in the short's title and copy.

INFERRED, not verified: I measured levels and frames and did not listen for delivery energy. 'Hype' rests on the text and on the CH1 opening being Mike's gear-3 hold. I did not watch IMG-2's drift or judge how the leak seams read in motion.
